memory_update.text: Keep AMAT as reference-only anchor for subsystem supplier mapping; do not let it crowd out lower-visibility subsystem names in later layers.

MKSI is a broad semicap subsystem candidate spanning vacuum, process control, plasma/reactive gas, photonics, motion, optics, vibration isolation, and packaging chemistry; large-cap size reduces underfollowed purity but node fit is strong.
AEIS is a direct RF/plasma-power and precision-control candidate; verify whether leading-edge AI logic/memory process complexity is increasing content per tool.
ICHR is a narrower and more underfollowed fluid-delivery subsystem candidate with high OEM customer concentration; this concentration is both a validation signal and a Layer 2 risk.
Layer 2 should add UCTT, ENTG, and possibly non-US-listed VAT Group and INFICON as peer checks, but they were excluded from this Layer 1B output to keep the candidate list at four.

The strongest version of the node thesis is not simply 'more WFE'; it is rising subsystem intensity per process step, driven by tighter tolerances in etch, deposition, advanced packaging, and leading-edge memory/logic.

node: Semiconductor equipment subsystems: vacuum, RF power, gas flow, measurement, motion control, and process-control components embedded inside larger wafer-fab tools
summary: Layer 1B expands the direct public-company universe around semiconductor-equipment subsystems. The two-lane map uses Applied Materials as a reference OEM/customer anchor, then prioritizes less obvious subsystem suppliers with direct exposure to vacuum/process control, RF/plasma power, and fluid-delivery subsystems. The strongest underfollowed candidates from this pass are MKS Instruments, Advanced Energy Industries, and Ichor Holdings. Key verification work for Layer 2 should focus on segment-level semiconductor exposure, OEM customer concentration, gross-margin durability, backlog/order recovery, and whether AI-driven leading-edge logic, memory, and advanced packaging capex is increasing subsystem intensity rather than merely pulling forward cyclical WFE demand.
